title: Accounting & UAE VAT
tagline: Bookkeeping, financial statements, VAT and corporate tax in the UAE: the numbers every business and freelancer must get right.

superpower.name: Numbers Pro
superpower.description: Keeps clean books and pays the right tax: fewer fines and better business decisions.

syllabus: Week 1: Bookkeeping: the accounting equation and double entry
Week 2: Financial statements: profit, balance sheet and cash flow
Week 3: UAE VAT: registration, invoices and returns
Week 4: Corporate tax, records and running the books

weeks.title: Bookkeeping Basics
weeks.objective: Record transactions correctly with double-entry bookkeeping.

slides.title: The Accounting Equation
slides.body: Every business balances: what it owns equals what it owes plus what belongs to the owners. Every transaction keeps this equation in balance.
bullets: Assets = Liabilities + Equity
Assets: cash, stock, equipment, money owed to you
Liabilities: loans, bills, money you owe
Equity: the owner's investment plus retained profit
slides.example:
You start a business with AED 50,000 of your savings and a AED 20,000 loan.
Assets (cash): AED 70,000
Liabilities (loan): AED 20,000
Equity (your money): AED 50,000
70,000 = 20,000 + 50,000. It balances.
slides.takeaway: If the equation doesn't balance, something's been recorded wrong.

slides.title: Double Entry: Debits and Credits
slides.body: Every transaction is recorded twice: a debit in one account and an equal credit in another. That's what keeps the books balanced.
bullets: Debits increase assets and expenses
Credits increase liabilities, equity and income
Total debits always equal total credits
Accrual accounting records income when earned and costs when incurred, not when cash moves
slides.takeaway: Two sides to every transaction: learn that and bookkeeping clicks.

lab.title: Bookkeeping Lab
lab.brief: Record 10 transactions for a small café's first month with double entry, then check the trial balance.
lab.deliverable: A journal and a balanced trial balance.
lab.proTip: Reconcile with the bank statement every month: it catches most mistakes.

caseStudy.scenario: You buy a AED 3,000 coffee machine on credit. How is it recorded?

options.text: Debit equipment (asset) AED 3,000; credit accounts payable (liability) AED 3,000.
options.explanation: An asset goes up, and so does what you owe.
No cash moved; you bought on credit.

options.text: Don't record it until you pay.
options.explanation: Under accrual accounting you record it when you get the machine.

weeks.title: Financial Statements
weeks.objective: Read and prepare the three statements that tell a business's story.

slides.title: Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow
slides.body: Three reports answer three questions: did we make money (P&L), what do we own and owe (balance sheet), and where did cash go (cash flow statement)? UAE companies generally follow IFRS.
bullets: P&L: revenue − cost of sales = gross profit; − expenses = net profit
Balance sheet: a snapshot of assets, liabilities and equity on one date
Cash flow: operating, investing and financing cash
Profit isn't cash: a profitable business can still run out of money
slides.example:
A café's month:
Revenue: AED 80,000
Cost of sales (food and drink): AED 26,000 → gross profit AED 54,000
Rent, salaries, utilities: AED 45,000 → net profit AED 9,000
But if AED 20,000 of sales are to corporate clients who haven't paid yet, cash is tight despite the profit.
slides.takeaway: Read all three together: profit, position and cash.

slides.title: Key Ratios
bullets: Gross margin % = gross profit ÷ revenue
Net margin % = net profit ÷ revenue
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities (above 1 is healthier)
Days receivable: how long customers take to pay
slides.takeaway: Watch margins and cash days monthly, not yearly.

lab.title: Statements Lab
lab.brief: From a trial balance, prepare a simple P&L and balance sheet, and calculate gross margin, net margin and the current ratio.
lab.proTip: Explain each number in one sentence: if you can't, you don't understand it yet.

caseStudy.scenario: A business shows a healthy profit but can't pay salaries this month. Most likely why?

options.explanation: Possible, but the usual cause is cash tied up.

options.text: Cash is tied up in unpaid customer invoices or stock.
options.explanation: Profit isn't cash: collections and stock absorb it.

options.text: Profit and cash are always the same.

weeks.title: UAE VAT
weeks.objective: Register, invoice and file VAT correctly.

slides.title: VAT Basics and Registration
slides.body: VAT was introduced in the UAE on 1 January 2018 at 5%, administered by the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) through the EmaraTax portal. Registration depends on your taxable supplies.
bullets: Mandatory registration: taxable supplies over AED 375,000 in the past 12 months (or expected in the next 30 days)
Voluntary registration: over AED 187,500
Standard rate 5%; some supplies are zero-rated (like exports and many education and healthcare services) or exempt (like residential rent)
A registered business gets a Tax Registration Number (TRN)
slides.takeaway: Track your rolling 12-month sales: crossing AED 375,000 means you must register.

slides.title: Invoices and Returns
slides.body: You charge VAT on sales (output tax), reclaim VAT on business purchases (input tax), and pay the FTA the difference, usually every quarter.
bullets: Tax invoices show your TRN, the VAT amount and the date
VAT payable = output tax − input tax
Returns are usually due within 28 days after the end of each tax period
Keep VAT records for at least 5 years
slides.example:
A quarter for a design agency:
• Sales AED 200,000 + 5% VAT = AED 10,000 output tax
• Business purchases with VAT invoices: AED 60,000 + AED 3,000 input tax
VAT payable to the FTA: 10,000 − 3,000 = AED 7,000
slides.takeaway: Only claim input VAT you can back up with a valid tax invoice.

lab.title: VAT Return Lab
lab.brief: From a quarter's sales and purchase invoices, calculate output tax, input tax and VAT payable, and spot invoices that can't be claimed.
lab.proTip: Reconcile your VAT account to the return before you submit.

caseStudy.scenario: A freelancer's sales over the last 12 months reached AED 410,000. What must they do?

options.explanation: VAT depends on taxable supplies, not on being a freelancer.

options.text: Register for VAT with the FTA within the deadline, because they're over AED 375,000.
options.explanation: Mandatory registration applies above the threshold.

options.text: Wait until they reach AED 1 million.

weeks.title: Corporate Tax and Running the Books
weeks.objective: Understand UAE corporate tax and keep books that pass any review.

slides.title: UAE Corporate Tax
slides.body: Corporate tax applies to business profits for financial years starting on or after 1 June 2023, also through the FTA.
bullets: 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000; 9% above that
Small Business Relief: businesses with revenue of AED 3 million or less can elect to be treated as having no taxable income (for eligible periods)
Qualifying free zone persons may get 0% on qualifying income
Register even if no tax is due; keep records for at least 7 years
slides.example:
Taxable income AED 900,000:
First AED 375,000 at 0% = AED 0
Remaining AED 525,000 at 9% = AED 47,250
Corporate tax due: AED 47,250
slides.takeaway: Register, keep records and know which rate applies to you.

slides.title: Monthly Close
slides.body: Good books are a habit: a short routine every month keeps you ready for VAT, tax, banks and investors.
bullets: Record all sales and costs with invoices
Reconcile every bank account
Review receivables and chase late payers
Produce a monthly P&L and compare with budget
slides.takeaway: Ten minutes a day on the books beats ten days of panic at year-end.

lab.title: Month-End Lab
lab.brief: Run a month-end close for a small business: reconcile the bank, chase two overdue invoices and produce a P&L.
lab.deliverable: A reconciliation, a P&L and two polite chase emails.
lab.proTip: Automate what you can: accounting software and bank feeds cut errors.

caseStudy.scenario: A startup earned AED 300,000 taxable profit this year. How much corporate tax?

options.explanation: The first AED 375,000 is taxed at 0%.

options.text: AED 0: it's within the 0% band, but they must still register and file.
options.explanation: Below AED 375,000 the rate is 0%; registration still applies.
No tax is due in the 0% band.
